title: Distributed Team Operating and Career Support Manual
author: Nina Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This manual defines how distributed teams at Redwood operate day-to-day, how managers and ICs should approach career development across time zones, and which benefits and internal tools are available to support people operations and onboarding. The aim is consistent, equitable experiences for teammates whether they are on-site, hybrid, or fully remote.

Scope
- Applies to all full-time and part-time Redwood employees and contractors engaged for >6 months.
- Covers collaboration norms, career ladder checkpoints, benefits alignment for life events, onboarding checklist, and internal tools access matrix.

Principles (short)
- Timezone-first collaboration: design meetings and handoffs with timezone impact in mind.
- Async-first default: prefer documented threads, short recorded updates, and clear owner/action items.
- Equitable benefit access: ensure parents, caregivers, and teammates in different jurisdictions get consistent support.
- Clear career pathways: transparency on expectations, artifacts, and timeline for promotions.

1) Collaboration and Meeting Guidelines
- Default meeting window: 10:00–16:00 UTC as the preferred range for cross-team meetings. Avoid all-hands outside this window unless pre-cleared.
- Meeting types and rules:
  - Standups: 15 minutes max, asynchronous update channel summary posted if attendees span >2 timezones.
  - Design reviews: shared pre-reads in Confluence 48 hours before meeting.
  - Deep work days: teams block at least one weekly deep-work day (no recurring meetings).
- Asynchronous practices:
  1. Create a short context blurb in the thread ("TL;DR + owner + requested outcome").
  2. Use Loom or recorded demos for 5–10 minute walkthroughs.
  3. Tag required reviewers and include a suggested deadline.

2) Role Expectations and Career Ladder (summary table)
| Level | Scope & Impact | Typical Tenure | Promotion Signals | Managerial Option |
|-------|----------------|----------------|-------------------|------------------|
| IC2   | Executes features, owns tickets | 0–2 years | Delivers consistent work, clear communication | Individual contributor |
| IC3   | Owns components, mentors juniors | 2–4 years | Reliable delivery, mentors, technical design contributions | May lead small projects |
| Senior| Cross-team influence, design leadership | 4+ years | Drives architecture, measurable impact, hires | IC or people manager path |
| Mgr   | Team health, outcomes, career growth | varies | Team delivery, 1:1 cadence, performance calibration | People leader |
- Promotion process (high level):
  1. Candidate prepares a promotion packet: summary of impact, examples aligned to checklist, feedback excerpts.
  2. Manager reviews and nominates to calibration panel.
  3. Calibration panel evaluates and returns decision within 28 days.
  4. If approved, HR coordinates new title, comp review, and announcement.

3) Onboarding and Early Career Support (30/90/180 checklist)
Table: Onboarding Quick Checklist
| Day range | Key outcomes | Tools & Owners |
|----------|--------------|---------------|
| 0–7     | Account access, team orientation, buddy assigned | IT: account provisioning; Buddy: team intro; People Ops: benefits kickoff |
| 8–30    | Complete product orientation, shadowing, first deliverable | Manager: 1:1 weekly; Eng DX: API keys & sandbox; Security: baseline training |
| 31–90   | Independent delivery, mid-review, career plan draft | Manager: 30/60/90 review; People Ops: comp & benefits review |
| 91–180  | Performance calibration, mentorship pairing | Manager & Mentor: growth plan, stretch assignment |

Onboarding notes:
- New hires receive a dedicated buddy for the first 90 days.
- Access SLA: IT aims to complete access provisioning within 48 hours of offer acceptance. Escalate to people-ops-access@redwood.ai if delayed.

4) Benefits and Life-Event Support
- Primary benefits (high-level summary): health, dental, retirement match, paid parental leave, flexible returnship, mental health stipend, and annual wellbeing stipend.
- Dependent & family care support:
  - Care stipend: up to $1,200/year for dependent care or caregiving-related expenses (prorated for part-time).
  - Parental leave: 18 weeks primary, 8 weeks secondary (local law may supersede; see HR policy for jurisdictional variations).
  - Adoption & fertility support: limited reimbursement per plan year; contact People Ops for eligibility.
- Short-term hardship and emergency leave: case-by-case support via People Ops emergency fund; use the confidential request form on the HR portal.

5) Internal Tools, Access, and Ownership
- Key systems and owners:
  - HRIS: BambooHR (People Ops) — new hire records, leave requests.
  - Single Sign-On: Okta (Eng Infra) — app access provisioning.
  - Confluence & Jira: Eng DX (Documentation & ticketing).
  - Slack: Communications (global channels & regional channels).
  - VPN & VPC: Eng Infra (private deploy teams).
- Access matrix (core roles):
| Persona | Confluence | Jira | Prod read-only | Admin |
|---------|-----------|------|----------------|-------|
| New hire | Read | Create issues | No | No |
| IC | Read/Edit | Create & transition | Scoped by role | No |
| Manager | Read/Edit | Manage sprints | Scoped by team | No |
| Infra Admin | Read/Edit | Admin | Full | Yes |

- Tooling onboarding flow (procedure):
  1. People Ops triggers Okta account and base group memberships.
  2. Eng DX grants Confluence and Jira space access via group sync.
  3. Manager requests any additional product sandboxes via eng-dx-request@redwood.ai.

6) Mentorship, Performance Reviews, and Development Stipends
- Mentorship: Employees may request a mentor via the mentorship program form. Mentors are matched quarterly.
- Performance cycles: There are two formal touchpoints per year (mid-year check-in and annual review). Continuous feedback is encouraged.
- Development stipend: $1,000/year per employee for conferences, books, courses; approval via People Ops.

7) Escalation and Support Contacts
- People Ops general: people-ops@redwood.ai
- Access issues: people-ops-access@redwood.ai
- Benefits & leaves: benefits@redwood.ai
- Emergency fund: confidential-form@redwood.ai

Appendices
A. Sample promotion packet checklist:
- Impact summary (1 page)
- 3–5 concrete examples mapped to ladder criteria
- Peer & stakeholder feedback (3–7 excerpts)
- Manager assessment (strengths, risks, recommendation)

B. Quick scripts and CLI snippets (example for sandbox access request)
- curl -X POST https://eng-dx.internal/api/requests -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"type":"sandbox","env":"staging","owner":"<your_email>"}'

Related policies and next steps
- See: Role framework and growth paths (related_pages above) for full ladder definitions and evaluation rubrics.
- People Ops will run quarterly office hours for managers on timezone-aware scheduling and equitable workloads.

Document ownership and updates
- Owner: People Ops (Nina Patel). Review cadence: annual or on major policy change.
- Feedback: Send suggested edits or requests for clarification to people-ops@redwood.ai with subject line: "Handbook feedback: Distributed Team Manual".

End of document.
